title: Enhancing Radiation Shielding Capabilities with Epoxy-Resin Composites Reinforced with Coral-Derived Calcium Carbonate Fillers
content: This study investigates the development and characterization of epoxy-resin composites reinforced with coral-derived calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) fillers, with a focus on enhancing their radiation shielding and mechanical properties. Leveraging the high calcium content and density of coral, these composites are proposed as a sustainable and lightweight alternative to conventional materials like lead. Composites were prepared by incorporating coral-derived CaCO₃ fillers at weight fractions of 0%, 25%, and 50% into an epoxy resin matrix. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analyses revealed that higher filler concentrations (50%) led to increased particle agglomeration, impacting matrix uniformity. Mechanical testing showed that while tensile and flexural strengths decreased with higher filler content, compressive strength improved significantly, reaching 135 MPa at 50% coral content. Radiation shielding evaluation demonstrated that increasing filler content enhanced attenuation performance, with the 50% coral composite achieving a 39.63% absorption rate at 60 kVp. Despite its lower shielding efficiency compared to lead, the composite provides a safer and more environmentally friendly alternative for moderate shielding applications. These findings highlight the potential of coral-derived CaCO₃ fillers in developing sustainable materials for radiation protection, with future work needed to optimize filler dispersion and explore hybrid material systems.
